title: Opaque token shear and regional failover playbook for rate-governor reliability
creator: Priya Nair
description: Design, implement, and operationalize a playbook to improve limiter and quota enforcement reliability across multi-region deployments. This work targets burst handling, tenant fairness, and graceful behavior during limiter outages and partial network partitions. The approach introduces an 'opaque-token shear' admission primitive, regional lease versioning, and a circuit-breaker policy that ties to SLO-driven error-budget burn signals.
motivation: Recent incidents showed two failure modes: (1) limiter control-plane outages causing global hard-stops for active tenants, and (2) unbounded tenant bursts causing SLO violations in adjacent regions. We need a practical engineering pattern that reduces blast radius, preserves fairness during bursts, and ensures predictable failover when limiters become unavailable.
proposal: Introduce a hybrid admission model: (A) short-lived opaque admission tokens issued by the regional rate-governor with epoch metadata (region, epoch-id, local-credit), (B) token-shearing to split large token grants into fixed microcredits for controlled consumption, (C) lease-versioned token mirroring between primary and standby regions with bounded staleness, and (D) an SLO-aware circuit breaker that degrades admission policy (soft-shed, priority-only, background-only) based on burn-rate and p99 latency signals. Implement per-tenant microcredit accounting with a capped local burst buffer and a fallback path that uses a service-tiered admission policy when a governor becomes unreachable.
acceptance_criteria: No production-facing 5xx spikes attributable to limiter failovers during simulated governor outages (chaos tests).
Preserve fairness: Jain's fairness index across top-100 tenants must remain >= 0.92 in 95th percentile synthetic burst tests after introducing microcredits.
SLO coupling: error-budget burn rate triggers circuit-breaker transitions within defined thresholds (see telemetry_signals) and transitions are recorded in tracing and console UI for operator action.

Controlled failover: standby region can accept mirrored tokens within configured staleness (<= 5s) and resume admissions with no more than 3x temporary increase in tail latency for 99th percentile requests for up to 60s during handover.
Runbook validated: on-call runbook executes deterministic steps to recover or rollback and is exercised in at least two live drills with postmortem notes linked.
implementation_notes: Admission token format: base64 opaque blob with fields [region, epoch_id, tenant_id_hash, microcredit_count, expiry_ts, signature]. Tokens are not interpreted by callers; they are validated by admission proxies.
Shearing policy: when issuing N tokens for a burst, the governor emits fixed-size microcredits (default 8 tokens of 16ms consumption footprint) to reduce single-shot drain on downstream executors.
Local burst buffer: each proxy keeps a leaky bucket of microcredits per tenant capped at X=512 credits and refills from the regional governor asynchronously with backpressure and lease checks.

Lease mirroring: primary region streams compact delta of token grants (epoched) to standby via a bounded at-least-once queue with sequence checks; standby replays grants into its local store tagged with source_epoch and local_epoch.

Circuit breaker thresholds: tie to error budget burn rate > 3x baseline or p99 generation latency > 2x SLO for 1m window to enter soft-shed; on hard trip, move to priority-only admissions for 5m then reevaluate.

Trace & audit: every admission decision emits trace span with token_epoch, remaining_credits, policy_version, and reason_code. Admission events are exported to Console with sampling and full sampling for P0 tenants.
Compatibility: keep existing token-bucket admission as fallback; new tokens can be toggled per-route via feature-flag for gradual rollout.
rollback_plan: Feature-flag gated rollout. If post-deploy checks surface increased user errors or fairness degradation, flip feature flag off (proxy-side fast path) to revert to legacy token-bucket. In parallel, trigger a governor restart to clear in-memory drift and rehydrate from authoritative store. Operators must annotate the incident and schedule a postmortem within 48 hours.
telemetry_signals: error_budget_burn_rate: per-customer 1m and 5m burn-rate (calculated from SLOs configured per route)
admission_fail_rate: fraction of admitted requests rejected due to token validation or staleness
p50/p95/p99_generation_latency: end-to-end latencies for generation requests
microcredit_spend_rate: credits consumed per tenant per minute
token_staleness_seconds: distribution of delay between primary grant and standby mirror
jains_fairness_index: computed across tenants for matched windowed bursts
governor_heartbeat: last-seen timestamp and queue lag metrics
testing_plan: Unit tests for token format parsing and signature verification (negative and positive cases).
Integration tests: governor <-> proxy handshake, microcredit accounting, and mirrored-lease application with sequence reordering injection.
Chaos experiment: kill primary governor mid-burst and measure admission continuity and latency in standby (automated via chaos harness).
Load tests: synthetic top-100 tenant bursts with varied skew to verify fairness index and tail latency bounds.
DR drill: multi-region failover drill scheduled in staging and then in a limited-production window with observers and rollback criteria.
